title: Globalization

source.name: Wikipedia — Globalization
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Globalization is the process of increasing interdependence and integration among the economies, markets, societies, and cultures of different countries worldwide. It can be attributed to a series of factors, including the reduction of barriers to international trade, the liberalization of capital movements, the development of transportation infrastructure, and the advancement of information and communication technologies. The term globalization first appeared in the early 20th century, but came into popular use in the 1990s to describe the growing international connectivity of the post–Cold War world.

Large-scale globalization began in the 1820s, and in the late 19th century and early 20th century drove a rapid expansion in the connectivity of the world's economies and cultures. The origins of globalization can be traced back to the 18th and 19th centuries, a period marked by significant advancements in transportation and communication technologies following the Industrial Revolution. These developments increased global interactions, supporting the growth of international trade and the exchange of ideas, beliefs, and cultures.

Between 1990 and 2010, globalization progressed rapidly, driven by the information and communication technology revolution that lowered communication costs, along with trade liberalization and the shift of manufacturing operations to emerging economies (particularly China). Academic literature commonly divides globalization into three major areas: economic globalization, cultural globalization, and political globalization.

Proponents of globalization point to economic growth and broader societal development as benefits, while opponents claim globalizing processes are detrimental to social well-being due to ethnocentrism, environmental consequences, and other potential drawbacks.

The word globalization was used in the English language as early as the 1930s, but only ever in the context of education, and the term failed to gain traction. Over the next few decades, the term was occasionally used by other scholars and media, but it was not clearly defined. One of the first uses of a term resembling the more common meaning and usage of the modern word was by French economist François Perroux in his essays from the early 1960s (in his French works he used the similar yet distinct term mondialisation, translated as mundialization). Theodore Levitt is sometimes inaccurately cited as having invented the term in the mid-1980s, although he can more confidently be credited with popularizing the term and bringing it into the mainstream business audience during that time.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT given as a factor behind globalization?
options: The development of faster communication technology
The growing use of one common language across the world
The lowering of barriers to trade between countries
The building of better transport links around the world
questions.explain: Đoạn 1 nêu: giảm rào cản thương mại, tự do hóa vốn, hạ tầng giao thông, công nghệ thông tin – truyền thông. Không có “một ngôn ngữ chung”.

questions.q: What does paragraph 2 suggest about the origins of globalization?
options: It began suddenly in the 1990s after the end of the Cold War
It started when the internet allowed people to talk across the world
It was a purely political process led by governments of large nations
It goes back to technical progress that followed the Industrial Revolution
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: nguồn gốc có thể truy về thế kỉ 18–19, khi giao thông và thông tin tiến bộ sau Cách mạng Công nghiệp; thuật ngữ mới phổ biến từ thập niên 1990 (đoạn 1).

questions.q: Which combination of developments speeded up globalization between 1990 and 2010?
options: Cheaper communication, freer trade and factories moving to emerging economies
Less contact between cultures and a rise in regional conflicts
The end of the Industrial Revolution and a fall in international trade
Higher taxes on imports, more local factories and slower communication
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: cuộc cách mạng ICT làm giảm chi phí liên lạc, tự do hóa thương mại và việc chuyển sản xuất sang các nền kinh tế mới nổi (đặc biệt Trung Quốc).

questions.q: What is the main objection of the opponents of globalization?
options: They think it spreads one single culture and removes all religion
They believe that it slows down the growth of national economies
They argue that it can harm social well-being and the environment
They feel that it makes international travel too expensive for people
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: người phản đối cho rằng quá trình toàn cầu hóa gây hại cho phúc lợi xã hội vì chủ nghĩa dân tộc hẹp hòi (ethnocentrism), hậu quả môi trường…

questions.q: In paragraph 5, “failed to gain traction” suggests that the word globalization
options: did not become widely accepted when it was first used
was used only by people who spoke French as a first language
was banned from use in newspapers and magazines
was strongly criticised by scholars in the education field
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: từ này xuất hiện từ thập niên 1930 nhưng “failed to gain traction”, tức không được dùng rộng rãi lúc đó.

questions.q: What does the writer say about Theodore Levitt?
options: He argued against using the term in business circles and in the media
He invented the word in the 1930s while he was writing about education
He translated the essays of François Perroux from French into English
He is wrongly named as its inventor, though he did spread the word in business
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: Levitt “sometimes inaccurately cited as having invented the term”, nhưng “can more confidently be credited with popularizing the term”.

questions.q: The word “globalization” was already in use in English long before it became popular.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: được dùng trong tiếng Anh từ thập niên 1930 (chỉ trong giáo dục) trong khi chỉ phổ biến từ thập niên 1990 (đoạn 1).

questions.q: François Perroux was in favour of globalization.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5 chỉ nói Perroux dùng một thuật ngữ gần nghĩa vào đầu thập niên 1960; không nói quan điểm của ông.

vocab.ex: Globalization is the process of increasing interdependence and integration among the economies

vocab.def: making rules or laws less strict
basic systems such as roads, railways and power supply

vocab.ex: the growing international connectivity of the post–Cold War world

vocab.def: a person who supports an idea or plan
vocab.ex: Proponents of globalization point to economic growth and broader societal development as benefits
opponents claim globalizing processes are detrimental to social well-being

vocab.def: the support or progress that an idea gets

the shift of manufacturing operations to emerging economies

str.vi: Người ủng hộ …, trong khi người phản đối …
str.ex: Proponents of globalization point to economic growth and broader societal development as benefits, while opponents claim globalizing processes are detrimental to social well-being
str.explain: Dùng while nối hai quan điểm đối lập, rất phổ biến trong văn viết học thuật.

str.vi: một giai đoạn được đánh dấu bởi …
str.ex: a period marked by significant advancements in transportation and communication technologies
str.explain: Cụm quá khứ phân từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ (rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ).

str.vi: được thúc đẩy bởi …, cùng với …
str.ex: driven by the information and communication technology revolution that lowered communication costs, along with trade liberalization
str.explain: Phân từ quá khứ nêu nguyên nhân; along with bổ sung các yếu tố đi kèm.

str.ex: he can more confidently be credited with popularizing the term
str.explain: credit someone with + V-ing: công nhận ai là người đã làm gì.
